angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 602,476 km at 152.03 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.5777 +/- 0.0270 mas (same row, RUWE 1.57): 152.03 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.866 +/- 0.031 solar radii from Addison et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019PASP..131k5003A/abstract): 602,476 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.895 +/- 0.077 solar masses from Addison et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019PASP..131k5003A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5180 +/- 190 K from Addison et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019PASP..131k5003A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Addison et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-2 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019PASP..131k5003A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-2.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.515, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
